caller.identity: node-specific group append caller of the realloc-insert helper

container_layout.note: The helper reads begin and end only; it never reads the capacity field. It writes begin, end and capacity_end at the end.

arguments.rdi: container pointer (begin at +0x00, end at +0x08, capacity end at +0x10)
arguments.rsi: insert position pointer, must lie in [begin, end]
arguments.rdx: pointer to the qword value to insert (the value stored is the qword loaded from this address, not the address itself)

size_rule.definition: size = (end - begin) >> 3, arithmetic shift on the wrapped 64-bit difference
size_rule.length_error_arm: size == 0x0fffffffffffffff calls __throw_length_error with the rodata string at 0x43d55a ('vector::_M_realloc_insert'), noreturn

capacity_rule.empty_container: end == begin: new capacity is 1 element (size + 1, capped at the maximum)
capacity_rule.nonempty_container: new capacity is min(2 * size, 0x0fffffffffffffff) elements
capacity_rule.doubling_overflow_arm: when 2 * size wraps below size (unsigned), the native code takes the max-bytes allocation path: operator new(0x7ffffffffffffff8), with the capacity end recorded as the new buffer plus that byte count; that byte count equals maximum * 8, so the capped path and the wrap path end at the same capacity (maximum), and the model returns the maximum for both
capacity_rule.note: The helper always allocates a fresh buffer; there is no in-place arm even when spare capacity exists. Callers invoke it on their full path (end == capacity end), e.g. call site 0x5f780ad, reached only after the caller's own end == capacity-end test at 0x5f7808b.

copy_steps_in_order: value = qword loaded from the rdx pointer
when (position - begin) > 0 (signed): memmove(new_buffer, old_begin, position - begin)
when (old_end - position) > 0 (signed): memcpy(destination_after_insert, position, old_end - position)
when old_begin != 0: operator delete(old_begin, old_capacity_end - old_begin)
store new_buffer to container +0x00, new_end to container +0x08, new_buffer + allocation_bytes to container +0x10

caller_shape.note: Two inspected call sites show the caller-side contract: the caller tests end against capacity end itself and calls this helper only on the full path, passing the container in rdi, the insert position in rsi, and a pointer to the value in rdx.
inspected_sites: 0x5f780ad (append at end: rsi = end, rdx = stack slot holding the value; caller test at 0x5f7808b)
0x5d9f0c0 (rdi = container, rsi = end, rdx = computed element pointer)

arguments.rdi: object holding the 24-byte group entries at +0xa98

caller_semantics.group_entry: 24-byte record at [object + 0xa98] + index * 24; its first three qwords are the element container (begin +0, end +8, capacity end +0x10)
steps_in_order: store the value argument to a stack slot (that slot's address is the helper's value pointer on the full path)
when end != capacity end (signed compare of pointers as addresses): store the value at end, advance end by 8, then increment the 32-bit field at value + 0xb0 by 1, return void
when end == capacity end: call the realloc-insert helper with (container, end, address of the stack slot holding the value), then increment the 32-bit field at value + 0xb0 by 1, return void
caller_semantics.note: The +0xb0 increment happens on both arms, after the store in either arm; the helper's own store is what places the value on the full path, and the caller never touches the element list again after the call.
caller_semantics.callers_of_the_caller: 3 direct calls and 1 tail jump, sites only (see census)
